name: when epsilon takes over, 2026-11-13
purpose: Follow-up to the figure-legend rerun: find the update at which sqrt(v) falls below epsilon, and how far Adam is from the L-infinity optimum at that update, as the Adam learning-rate constant c, the exponent a, epsilon and the dataset change
status: Designed after all earlier results were known. Exploratory material for the report; not shown on the slides.
datasets: results/2026-11-05/datasets (same ten PCG64 datasets, same initial vectors, same selected seed 2)
loss_note: Averaged over the 50 samples, as in eq. 3.1 and protocol_legend.json.
c_values_note: c = 1 is the legends' value; the others are a factor of about 3 apart on each side.
tracked_thresholds_note: In runs with epsilon = 0, the update at which sqrt(v) first falls below each threshold is recorded; epsilon does not change these runs, so they show where on Adam's own path a given epsilon would start to matter.
takeover_definition: After every update, sqrt(v_j) at its real size (sqrt(v_scaled) * e^(-scale)) is compared with epsilon. 'first' is the first update with sqrt(v_j) < epsilon for at least one of the 50 coordinates; 'all' is the first update with sqrt(v_j) < epsilon for all 50 coordinates at once.
trajectory_kept: selected seed, suite c only (gzip CSV)
arithmetic: run_matched.adam_step unchanged: common exponential rescaling of the Adam moments, epsilon at its real size (epsilon*e^scale in the rescaled denominator), no clamp
